messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection change I see a p95 tail jump on prefill->decode handoff. Dash: https://perf.redwood/s/handshake
Maya Patel: ugh. numbers?
Alex Chen: Quick snapshot from prod profile (last 30m):\n```
phase=init(prefill) avg_batch=48 avg_wait=6.2ms handoff_missed=312
phase=gen(decode) avg_batch=6 avg_wait=2.1ms stall_spill=47 token_budget_exhaust=19\n```
Diego Rivera: model(s)? seems like KV-warmup could make prefill bigger and then decode can't catch up.
Alex Chen: Mostly affects long-context convo models (8k/32k), and requests with big prefill prompts. Not huge on small chat. Looks like batching is forming huge prefill windows then decode consumers starve.
Samir Gupta: thinking: add a microphase windowing heuristic so prefill will cap per-window tokens and let decode steal earlier. Something like: window_ms=8, token_cap_per_window=256, allow_spillover=1. Also emit backpressure signal to queue manager.
perf-bot: build/ci-perf: canary run with microphase-window enabled showed 8% p95 reduction but 2% throughput loss (stage: canary). See job 2026-03-17/ci-4287
Maya Patel: can you paste the exact config change to test? i'll spin a canary.
Alex Chen: patch we used:\n```
serving.scheduler: \n  microphase_window_ms: 8\n  prefill_token_cap: 256\n  prefill_spillover: true\n  allow_decode_claim: true\n```
kubectl patch ... will toggle `serving.scheduler.microphase_window_ms`
Diego Rivera: also check kernel selection: when seq_len>1024 we accidentally picked the wide-kernel which inflates prefill work. fallback to f16-narrow kernel for prefill-only batches might help. Pseudo: `if phase==prefill and seq>1024: prefer_kernel=f16_narrow`.
Samir Gupta: note: that fallback can cause KV cache thrash if kernels change layout; recommend pinning KV layout or warm KV after kernel swap: `kv_warmup=enabled, kv_warmup_samples=10`.
Alex Chen: Action items: 1) Maya run canary with microphase config and monitor tail + throughput 2) Diego try kernel-fallback patch in branch and run synthetic long-context 3) Samir add backpressure metric + expose `prefill_spillover` flag in console 4) hold full kernel swap on prod until canary stable. I'll post a short runbook. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: on it, starting canary now. will report p50/p95 in ~20m.
perf-bot: perf/alert: rolling window anomaly detected for handshake_latency p95 at 2026-03-17T14:12:23Z (+12%).
Alex Chen: thanks — will follow up with logs and traces once canary finishes.
